findings.evidence: grep: `abbrev filtrationPreviousRestricted` (Filtration.lean:156) vs `abbrev previousRestricted` (WordFiltration/AssociatedGraded.lean:81); `abbrev FiltrationGradedPiece ... := filtration Q k ⧸ filtrationPreviousRestricted Q k` (Filtration.lean:194) vs `abbrev GradedPiece f k := wordFiltration f k ⧸ previousRestricted f k` (AssociatedGraded.lean:107); the diff removes `@[simp]` from the four Clifford lemmas precisely because the generic ones now fire on them.
findings.fix: Delete the Clifford-facing duplicates and migrate their remaining uses (ExteriorFiltration.lean:94,96,111; FiltrationGradedEquiv.lean:89-94,103-104,125,172; PBW.lean:55-56,62,...; Filtration.lean:411-505) to `TauCeti.Algebra.wordFiltration.previousRestricted (ι Q)` / `GradedPiece (ι Q)` / `wordFiltrationPrevious_*` — or, if the Clifford names are meant to stay canonical, do not introduce the generic `previousRestricted` layer duplicating them.
findings.issue: Making `filtration`/`filtrationPrevious`/`filtrationPreviousRestricted` `abbrev`s turns the Clifford-facing names into exact reducible duplicates of the new generic ones, and the PR keeps both: `filtrationPreviousRestricted` (:156) = `wordFiltration.previousRestricted (ι Q)`, `mem_filtrationPreviousRestricted_iff` (:166) = `mem_previousRestricted_iff`, `filtrationPreviousRestricted_zero` (:177) = `previousRestricted_zero`, `filtrationPreviousRestricted_succ` (:188) = `previousRestricted_succ`, `FiltrationGradedPiece` (:194) = `GradedPiece (ι Q)`; likewise `filtration_zero`, `filtration_one`, `filtrationPrevious_zero`, `filtrationPrevious_succ` versus the generic `wordFiltration_*` lemmas. The docstrings say so outright ("the generic ... is the simp lemma ...; this Clifford-facing name is for `rw`"), and PBW.lean now mixes the two vocabularies in one file (`gradedMul (ι Q) i j x y` applied to `x : FiltrationGradedPiece Q i`).

findings.evidence: grep AssociatedGraded.lean:224-233, 247-259: bodies are literally `(gradedOne_def f).symm` and `(gradedAlgebraMap₀_apply f r).symm`; naming conventions: a theorem name describes its conclusion read from the conclusion outward.
findings.fix: Name the reversed simp lemmas after their LHS, e.g. `mk_one_eq_gradedOne` and `mk_algebraMap_eq_gradedAlgebraMap₀` (or drop them and use `(gradedOne_def _).symm` at the call sites).
findings.issue: `gradedOne_mk` (:230) and `gradedAlgebraMap₀_mk` (:255) are proved as `(gradedOne_def f).symm` and `(gradedAlgebraMap₀_apply f r).symm` — the same statements as `gradedOne_def` (:224) and `gradedAlgebraMap₀_apply` (:247), only reversed. The names also read backwards: their LHS head is `Submodule.Quotient.mk`, not `gradedOne`/`gradedAlgebraMap₀`, so `gradedOne_mk` parses as an application `gradedOne (mk _)` that is ill-typed.

findings.evidence: grep -n "filtered" TauCeti/Algebra/WordFiltration/AssociatedGraded.lean → lines 110, 160, 223, 229; the deleted file read "Clifford degree filtration" / "Clifford unit" at the same positions.
findings.fix: Say "the word filtration of `f`", "the associated graded of the word filtration", and "the unit of `A`".
findings.issue: Docstrings retain a mechanical "Clifford" → "filtered" substitution and now name the object wrongly: "the filtered degree filtration" (:110), "the filtered associated graded algebra" (:160), "the quotient class of the filtered unit" (:223, :229). There is no "filtered degree filtration"; the object is the word filtration of `f`, and its unit is the unit of `A`.

summary: The PR leaves a second, Clifford-specific name for every declaration the new generic API replaces, so the post-PR surface carries two names for each of the same reducibly-identical objects; two new `_mk` lemmas are also literal `.symm` duplicates whose names state the reverse of their conclusion.
